sections.title: People & Politics
sections.description: Important developments in governments, societies and the people shaping the world.

cards.title: Israeli Military Investigates 254 Incidents, Discloses Outcomes in Only 28 Cases
cards.content: The Israeli military has been accused of killing or injuring people in Gaza Lebanon the occupied West Bank and Israel but has not publicly disclosed the outcomes of investigations into most of these incidents. BBC Verify found 254 incidents where the Israeli military said it was investigating but only 28 of these had publicly disclosed outcomes. The investigations have been ongoing for years with some incidents dating back to 2023. Many of these incidents involve the killing or injury of civilians including women and children. The Israeli military has said it takes allegations of harm seriously but critics say the lack of transparency in investigations undermines accountability and perpetuates a culture of impunity.

cards.title: Australian Woman Charged with Poisoning Colleague's Curry with Snail Pellets
cards.content: An Australian woman was charged with poisoning her colleague's curry with snail pellets. The woman allegedly laced the curry with the poison which can cause serious injury or death after visiting a chemical storage shed. The colleague tasted the curry and noticed something was off so they handed it over to detectives who identified the substance. The accused will face court on November 5th.

cards.title: Australian Government Introduces Laws to Give Users Control Over Online Content
cards.content: The Australian government is introducing new laws to give people control over the content they see on social media and streaming services. The proposed law would force big tech companies to let users choose what type of content they see rather than relying on algorithms that send them recommended content. This isn't a new idea as other countries have already tried to do something similar. The goal is to give people more control over what they see online and reduce the spread of misinformation.

sections.title: Science and technology
sections.description: Discover breakthroughs in science, space, computing and emerging technology.

cards.title: Bank of America Hires Thousands to Fix Software Flaws
cards.content: Bank of America has hired thousands of contractors to fix software problems after an artificial intelligence model called Mythos found many old flaws. The bank's CEO Brian Moynihan said they rushed to patch up their systems in the second quarter and spent a couple hundred million dollars on it. He's reassuring investors that this spending increase is temporary and will decrease over time.

cards.title: ASML Sees Strong Demand for Chip-Making Machines in 2029 and 2030.
cards.content: ASML a Dutch company that makes special machines for making computer chips has seen its customers ask about buying those machines for 2029 and 2030. This news is good for investors because it shows that customers are planning ahead and expect to keep making a lot of chips.

cards.title: Elephant tooth fossil yields insights into ancient environment of early humans.
cards.content: A giant elephant's tooth has helped scientists learn about the environment that supported early humans around 700000 years ago. The tooth found in Israel belongs to an ancient elephant species and provides clues about the landscape back then. Researchers used special techniques to study the tooth and surrounding fossils including stone tools made by early humans. They found that the area had a lot of water vegetation and wildlife making it a good place for animals and humans to live. This information helps scientists understand how humans and animals responded to changes in their environment and how these changes shaped human populations.

sections.title: Health & wellness
sections.description: Medical research, public health and discoveries that affect everyday wellbeing.

cards.title: Scots struggle to access weight loss treatments despite three-year approval
cards.content: Fewer than 800 Scots have received NHS prescriptions for weight loss treatments like Mounjaro and Wegovy despite them being approved three years ago. Most health boards in Scotland don't offer the treatment specifically for weight loss and instead it's only available through small pilot schemes. This has led some doctors to describe the situation as "discriminatory" and widened health inequalities.

cards.title: Kenya Confirms Second Ebola Case, 39-Year-Old Man in Quarantine
cards.content: Kenya has confirmed a second case of Ebola 10 days after a businessman died of the virus. The new patient is a 39-year-old man who is a close relative of the first case and was already in quarantine when he fell ill. He was in quarantine because he was a contact of the first case and detecting his illness early improved his chances of recovery.

cards.title: Boy Kibble Diet Gains Popularity for High-Protein Convenience
cards.content:
Here is a summary of the news article in one natural paragraph

Boy kibble is a way of eating that has become popular on social media where people strip meals back to basics to get high protein and convenience. It's a batch-cooked meal typically made with rice and ground meat with some people adding avocado for healthy fat. The diet has been popular among men especially those looking to increase their fitness as it provides a reliable way to meet protein goals. However experts warn that the diet can be imbalanced with too much protein and not enough vegetables and recommend adding some variety to the meals.

sections.title: Environment
sections.description: Climate, oceans, ecosystems and the changing planet around us.

cards.title: Zimbabwe Prepares for Potential Drought with $500 Million Reserve
cards.content: Zimbabwe is preparing for a potential drought by setting up a $500 million reserve of cash and grain. This is because some weather experts think El Niño a natural weather pattern might cause a drought that would affect the country's food. The country's Cabinet had already agreed on a plan to get ready for this and make sure people have enough food and their livelihoods are safe.

cards.title: African Nations Urged to Prioritize Carbon Reduction Efforts
cards.content: A new report suggests African countries should choose which areas to focus on when it comes to removing carbon dioxide from the atmosphere. This approach would balance helping the environment with local development needs. Some methods like using charcoal or rocks could create jobs support farming and help restore ecosystems. However these benefits aren't guaranteed and projects need to be carefully planned to make sure they're a good use of resources and don't harm the environment.

cards.title: Indonesia suffers worst wildfire season on record with 1.06 million hotspots
cards.content: Indonesia has had a severe wildfire season with over 1.06 million hotspots detected since October 14. This is worse than the previous worst year 2019 when there were 885000 hotspots. The dry conditions caused by Super El Niño have made it harder to control the fires and increased the risk of more outbreaks. Smoke from the fires has spread to neighboring countries causing poor air quality and health concerns.

sections.title: Entertainment
sections.description: Stories from film, music, sports, culture and the world of entertainment.

cards.title: La Bola Negra Nominated for Best Picture Academy Awards
cards.content: A film called La Bola Negra is a contender for the Academy Awards' best picture prize. The movie tells three stories of gay men across a century in Spain exploring themes of love repression and self-punishment. The film has received critical acclaim and is a commercial hit in Spain. It's known for its beautiful visuals complex storyline and courage in showing sexual desire. The directors Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi have been praised for their work and the film's cast including Álvaro Lafuente Calvo and Carlos González have also received recognition.

cards.title: Lena Dunham Revives Girls for Limited Run with Original Cast
cards.content: Lena Dunham the creator of the popular TV show Girls announced that the show will return for a limited run after a 10-year hiatus. The revival will feature five episodes and reunite the original cast including Allison Williams Jemima Kirke Zosia Mamet and Andrew Rannells. Dunham said she's been missing the characters and that they started talking to her again around her 40th birthday. The show will explore what's happened to the characters since they were in their 20s.

cards.title: Rob Brydon Voices New Animated "The Baddies" Adaptation
cards.content: Welsh actor Rob Brydon is voicing a new animated adaptation of the popular children's book "The Baddies" over the Christmas period. The story follows a troll a ghost and a witch as they try to steal a blue spotty hanky from a brave little girl. Brydon will be joined by Gavin and Stacey co-stars Sheridan Smith and Alison Steadman as well as Hammed Animashaun Robyn Cara and Francesca Mills. The half-hour special celebrates kindness and standing up to bullies and features beautiful animation.

sections.title: economy
sections.description: Markets, businesses, trade and economic changes shaping the global economy.

cards.title: Anthropic Sees 45% Revenue Hike to $16.8 Billion
cards.content: Artificial intelligence company Anthropic saw its revenue jump by 45% to $16.8 billion in the last three months. This is a big increase from previous quarters and the company is preparing to list its stock on the market later this year.

cards.title: Teacher Struggles to Make Ends Meet in West Tennessee Amid Rising Costs
cards.content: Kathryn Vaughn a 46-year-old teacher is struggling to make ends meet in West Tennessee. She works three jobs to support her family of four including as a primary school art teacher but still finds it hard to afford basic necessities like food and gas. Vaughn's story is echoed by others across the US who are feeling the pinch of rising costs and increasing prices.

cards.title: Companies fined £6m for misleading sales tactics
cards.content: Wayfair Appliances Direct and Gold's Gym have been fined a total of £6m by the Competition Markets Authority for using misleading sales tactics. Wayfair was fined £4.8m for advertising products as if they would disappear quickly while Appliances Direct was fined £1.2m for automatically enrolling customers in services without their permission. Gold's Gym was fined £45000 for not clearly showing the total price of gym memberships. The companies will have to refund customers a total of £440000 with thousands of Appliances Direct customers and 726 Gold's Gym customers expected to receive refunds.
